column1: Two types of predictability in MS Azure Well-Architechted Framework ?/?
column3: Performance predictability ensures that your applications consistently meet performance requirements under varying loads; Cost predictability helps you manage and forecast your cloud expenses effectively.

column1: Term for feature that can deploy additional resources to meet the demand
column3: Autoscaling automatically adjusts the number of active servers or resources based on current demand; ensuring optimal performance and cost-efficiency.

column1: Feature of the cloud to help better plan resource deployments
column3: Data analytics tools can analyze historical usage patterns and predict future resource needs; helping organizations optimize their cloud deployments.

column1: Two tools they list to better estimate cost of potential cloud spend? (acronym/full name)
column3: The Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) Calculator helps estimate the cost savings of migrating to Azure; The Pricing Calculator allows you to estimate the cost of Azure services based on your projected usage.

column1: The main type of template that ensures all deployed resources meet standards/requirements
column3: ARM templates are JSON files that define the infrastructure and configuration for your Azure solution; (Bicep is a newer; friendlier language that compiles down to ARM templates)

column1: What feature looks for and flags resources that are out of compliance?
column3: Auditing continuously monitors your resources to ensure they comply with organizational policies and standards; flagging any deviations for review and remediation.

column1: Term for framework of policies/controls that ensure cloud resources are used properly & in compliance?
column3: Governance encompasses the policies; processes; and controls that ensure effective and compliant use of cloud resources within an organization.

column1: Three things where responsibility can vary with PaaS (???/???/???)
column3: networking settings and connectivity within your cloud environment; Applications (and security); and identity/directory infrastructure.

column1: An extra set of benefits of PaaS besides its use as a Development Framework ?/?
column3: Think of it this way: Analytics is like being a detective looking for clues and patterns; while BI is like being a manager using reports to make business decisions.

column1: Microsoft's cloud based ID & Access management services new name
column3: formerly Azure Active Directory (Azure AD); Entra ID provides identity and access management services for cloud-based applications and resources.

column1: For business and enterprise users; Microsoft 365 operates as a ? ? service
column3: This means while Microsoft manages the infrastructure; your organization controls how services are configured and used.

column1: What did Office 365 evolve from?
column3: Business Productivity Online Suite (BPOS) was the predecessor to Office 365; it provided hosted versions of Microsoft Exchange; SharePoint; and Lync services.

column1: Microsofts platform that includes Intune and EntraID (Acronym)
column3: Enterprise Mobility + Security (EMS) is a suite of tools that includes Intune for device management and Entra ID for identity and access management.

column1: Two intelligent tools built into Word 365 ?/?
column3: Editor provides advanced grammar and style suggestions to improve writing quality; Researcher helps users find credible sources and content for their documents.

column1: How copilot in Excel can help?
column3: They specifically say 'insights; trends and visualizations' from your data.

column1: Two intelligent tools in PowerPoint 365 ?/?
column3: Designer suggests design layouts and visual enhancements for slides; Speaker Coach provides feedback on presentation delivery; including pacing; tone; and use of filler words.

column1: How Copilot in OneNote can help (generally) ?/?
column3: Copilot can help summarize notes; organize content; and generate ideas for better note-taking.

column1: Copilot in OneNote can also help by creating ?/?
column3: Copilot can assist in creating lists; plans; and action items based on your notes.

column1: The main thing they say Copilot does in Outlook besides writing stuff?
column3: Copilot can help summarize lengthy email threads; highlight key points; and suggest responses.

column1: View types in MS Project? (the weird named two) ?/?
column3: Kanban view provides a visual way to manage tasks using boards and cards; Gantt view displays tasks along a timeline; showing dependencies and progress.

column1: Microsoft Project is built on the ?
column3: Microsoft Project leverages the Power Platform to enhance project management capabilities; including automation; data analysis; and custom app development.

column1: Three key elements of Microsoft Loop ?/?/?
column3: Components are individual units of content that can be shared and collaborated on; Pages are flexible canvases that organize components and content; Workspaces are collaborative environments where teams can work together on projects and ideas.

column1: A smart information tracking app to organize information and work?
column3: Microsoft Lists helps users track information; organize work; and collaborate with team members through customizable lists and views. Track item history with versions.

column1: What is the app for scheduling meetings and stuff called?
column3: Microsoft Bookings is an online scheduling tool that allows businesses to manage appointments; bookings; and customer interactions efficiently.

column1: Provides a simple and visual way for teams to organize their work; task-based initiatives
column3: Microsoft Planner enables teams to create; assign; and track tasks using visual boards; making it easy to manage projects and collaborate effectively.

column1: New Copilot feature to co-create content in real time alongside Teammates and AI
column3: Pages turns Copilot responses into editable; shared workspaces where you can seamlessly build on ideas by adding content from Copilot; your own files; and even web-based insights.

column1: Sharepoint feature to Create; share and manage live and on-demand videos within a small team; or across an organization
column3: Microsoft Stream allows users to upload; share; and manage video content securely within their organization; facilitating communication and collaboration through video.

column1: In Teams; A Team is a collection of ?/?/?
column3: People are the members of the team; Content includes files; documents; and resources shared within the team; Tools refer to apps and integrations. Teams can be public or private.

column1: A Team has a limit of up to how many members (at the time of the MS-900 material)?
column3: The new number appears to be 25000 members as of 2024 but the MS-900 material states 10000.

column1: Three types of Teams Channels ?/?/?
column3: Standard channels are open to all team members; Private channels restrict access to specific members; Shared channels allow collaboration with people outside the team.

column1: Files are shared in a Team Channel from what Tab/Stored Where?
column3: The Files tab in a Teams channel provides access to documents and files shared within that channel; these files are stored in a SharePoint site associated with the team.

column1: Copilot in Teams can give highlights from past ?/?/? days
column3: Copilot can summarize key points; action items; and decisions from meetings held in the past 1; 7; or 30 days.

column1: Copilot CANNOT reference ?/?/? shared in a chat thread
column3: It cannot reference Images; Loop Components; or Files shared in a chat thread.

column1: Loop components are ?/? content blocks
column3: Loop components are portable/live-updating content blocks that can be shared and collaborated on across Microsoft 365 apps. (eg A table; list; task list; or paragraph)

column1: Three ways users can join a Teams meeting ?/?/?
column3: Users can join a Teams meeting via a direct link; through their calendar invite; or by dialing in using a phone.

column1: Audio conferencing allows up to ? phone attendees?
column3: Audio conferencing in Microsoft Teams allows up to 1000 phone attendees to join a meeting by dialing in using a provided phone number.

column1: Two features of Teams premium ?/?
column3: Real-time translation provides live captions in multiple languages during meetings; Meeting recap offers a summary of key points; action items; and decisions made during the meeting.

column1: Net app in Teams to get list of future/past meetings?
column3: The Meet app in Teams provides users with a consolidated view of their upcoming and past meetings; allowing easy access to join or review meeting details. Can also get meeting recordings/transcripts.

column1: View-Only capabilities in Meetings is for participants from ?-?
column3: Audio; Video and Screen sharing are allowed for up to 1000 participants; View-Only capabilities allow an additional 19000 participants to watch the meeting without interacting.

column1: What tool is kinda like your own Enterprise youtube thing? Microsoft ?
column3: Microsoft Stream is an enterprise video service that allows organizations to upload; share; and manage video content securely within their organization; facilitating communication and collaboration through video.

column1: From a meeting YMicrosoft 365 Copilot can organize your discussion points into a ? table
column3: Copilot can format discussion points into a Markdown table; making it easy to organize and present information clearly.

column1: Integration with third-party services in teams can be done through incoming and outgoing ?/?
column3: Think of webhooks as automated messengers that send notifications between apps; connectors are more pre-packaged integrations with popular services; easier to set up

column1: EXP meaning?
column3: Microsoft Viva is an integrated employee experience platform (EXP) that empowers people and teams to be their best.

column1: Which Viva tool is kind of like 'Facebook for your company'?
column3: Viva Engage (formerly Yammer) is a social networking platform for organizations with posts; comments; likes; and communities - basically corporate social media.

column1: a Viva app described as a 'centralized campaign management'; publishing; and reporting app for corporate communicators'
column3: Viva Amplify helps organizations create; distribute; and measure the impact of internal communications campaigns effectively. (publishing workflows/track and measure analytics too)

column1: The three levels of insights available in Viva Insights ?/?/?
column3: Personal insights help individuals improve productivity and well-being; Manager insights provide team-level analytics to support effective management; Leader insights offer organizational-level data to inform strategic decisions.

column1: What Viva tool is for formal employee feedback and measuring engagement (large scale)?
column3: Viva Glint enables organizations to gather formal employee feedback; measure engagement; and gain insights to improve workplace culture and performance.

column1: What Viva tool is survey solution for managers and project leads for quick feedback?
column3: quick feedback from their teams to understand experiences and recommendations. Data remains confidential to managers and project leads.

column1: Two Onedrive features of that can reverse decisions?
column3: Version History allows users to view and restore previous versions of files; Data Recovery helps recover deleted files from the recycle bin within a specified retention period.

column1: Three security features of OneDrive?
column3: OneDrive uses encryption to protect data both in transit and at rest; Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) adds an extra layer of security during sign-in; Ransomware detection and recovery helps identify and recover files affected by ransomware attacks.

column1: Type of Teams meeting is focused on two-way interaction where presenter and participants have clear roles?
column3: Webinars are designed for larger audiences where presenters share content and participants can interact through Q&A; chat; and polls.

column1: The name of the security model that 365 Endpoint Management tools use?
column3: The Zero Trust security consists of three guiding principles: Verify explicitly; use least privilege access; and assume breach.

column1: Something Intune can automate deployment for that isnt app/OS?
column3: Intune can automate the deployment of security and configuration policies to ensure devices comply with organizational standards.

column1: Something Intune offers that is specifically for USERS (not IT)?
column3: The Company Portal app allows users to securely access corporate resources; install apps; and manage their devices enrolled in Intune.

column1: Basically an on-prem predecessor to Intune? (Acronym)
column3: System Center Configuration Manager (SCCM) is an on-premises management solution that provides similar capabilities to Intune; including software deployment; patch management; and device configuration.

column1: If you need to manage a combination of both cloud and on-premises endpoints; you can use:
column3: Three main features of Cloud Attach listed: [Co-management; Tenant Attach; and Endpoint Analytics] Cloud Attach allows extending on-prem capabilities to cloud-managed devices.

column1: Two AUTO Endpoint management tools: Auto ?/?
column3: Autopilot simplifies device provisioning and setup for new devices; Autopatch automates the deployment of Windows and Office updates to ensure devices stay secure and up-to-date.

column1: Endpoint Mgmt tool where can add devices/users/roups; create/manage policies; and monitor policies using report data
column3: The Intune Admin Center is a web-based portal that provides a centralized interface for managing devices; users; and policies within Microsoft Intune.

column1: The only cloud solution that delivers multi-session user access on Windows
column3: Azure Virtual Desktop allows multiple users to access a single Windows machine simultaneously; providing a cost-effective solution for remote desktop and application delivery. (Win365 = one user)

column1: What technology does Azure VD use to manage multiple desktops/users?
column3: FSLogix is a set of technologies that enhance user profile management in virtual desktop environments; enabling faster logins; improved application performance; and seamless user experiences. (It containers user profiles)

column1: Windows 365/Azure Virtual Desktop have ?/? cost structures
column3: Windows 365 uses a fixed pricing model based on the number of users and selected configurations; Azure Virtual Desktop employs a variable pricing model based on actual resource consumption; such as compute; storage; and networking.

column1: How often are Feature updates released?
column3: It used to be twice a year but now they are released once a year (in the second half of the year).

column1: How often are Quality updates released?
column3: <non-security releases or combined security + non-security releases.> Typically on the second Tuesday of each month (Patch Tuesday).

column1: New features are delivered to the Windows Insider community during the development cycle through process called ?
column3: This allows organizations to see what Microsoft is developing and start testing (a choice of release channel). Microsoft recommends that all organizations have at least a few devices enrolled in this program.

column1: Long-term servicing channel receives new updates every ? years
column3: The Long-Term Servicing Channel (LTSC) is designed for specialized devices and scenarios where stability and long-term support are critical; it receives feature updates every 2-3 years.

column1: A group of users or devices that receive a particular update together
column3: Deployment Rings allow organizations to gradually roll out updates to different groups of users or devices; eg ring structure: Preview > Limited > Broad

column1: Run from the command line and uses a configuration file to determine what settings to apply when deploying Office:
column3: The Office Deployment Tool (ODT) allows administrators to customize and manage Office installations; Install from the Office Content Delivery Network (CDN) or a local source.

column1: Windows 365 is a cloud-based service that automatically creates
column3: Windows 365 automatically provisions and manages Cloud PCs; providing users with a personalized Windows experience accessible from any device with an internet connection.

column1: What is the term for the new mode of continuously updating windows with Feature and Quality updates?
column3: Windows as a Service (WaaS) is a model where Windows is continuously updated with new features and improvements; rather than receiving major updates every few years.

column1: Viva Insights in Teams/Web: Recommended for you/Your progress/Inspiration Library are on ? tab?
column3: The Home tab in Viva Insights provides personalized recommendations; tracks your progress; and offers access to the Inspiration Library for resources to enhance productivity and well-being.

column1: Viva Insights in Teams/Web: Take Action/Track Progress/Act With Intention/Reflect on Emotions are on ? tab?
column3: The Wellbeing tab in Viva Insights focuses on helping users manage their work-life balance; improve work habits and manage time effectively.

column1: Viva Insights in Teams/Web: Meeting habits/category insights/effectiveness surveys/plans/Suggested tasks are on ? tab?
column3: Insights and tools related to meetings; time management; and tasks to help you improve meeting effectiveness; productivity; and collaboration.

column1: Viva Insights in Teams/Web tab to get better understanding of who is top collaborators/time you spend collabing with them?
column3: The Teamwork tab in Viva Insights provides insights into collaboration patterns; helping users understand who they work with most frequently and how they spend their time collaborating.

column1: Acronym for the 4 key metric categories tracked on Copilot dashboard?
column3: Readiness; Adoption; Impact and Sentiment. These metrics are aggregated at either the tenant or user level; depending on your organization's licensing.

column1: Two views in m365 admin center (admin.microsoft.com) ?/?
column3: Simplified view helps smaller organizations manage their most common tasks such as managing users; subscriptions; and Teams. The dashboard view includes more complex settings and tasks.

column1: Address of the Microsoft 365 User Portal?
column3: Access (licensed) Apps; Manage Account Settings/Password Resets; Install Office Apps(if admin allows); Do MFA options and more

column1: Reports in the M365 Admin center are available for the last ?/?/?/? days
column3: You need to have the right admin permissions to be able to view these reports.

column1: This score reflects People and Technology experience measurements and can be compared Organizations similar to yours
column3: Adoption score provides insights into your organization's digital transformation journey through its use of Microsoft 365 and the technology experiences that support it.

column1: A percentage that acts as indicator for how aligned you are with Microsoft's security best practice recommendations
column3: helps you to objectively measure your identity security posture; plan identity security improvements; and review the success of your improvements.

column1: An identity for an application that has been registered with MS Entra ID
column3: The service principal enables core features such as authentication and authorization of the application to resources that are secured by the Microsoft Entra tenant.

column1: What type of 'Workload Identity' can be System or User assigned?
column3: Managed identities provide an identity for applications to use when connecting to Azure resources that support Microsoft Entra authentication and can be used without any extra cost.

column1: Specific name for one method MS provides for inter-directory provisioning
column3: It accomplishes this by using the Microsoft Entra cloud provisioning agent. The agent provides a lightweight inter-directory provisioning experience that acts as a bridge between Microsoft Entra ID and Active Directory.

column1: The standard used to automate the exchanging of user or group identity information between identity domains
column3: System for Cross-domain Identity Management (SCIM) is an open standard that enables the automation of user provisioning and deprovisioning across different identity domains; It is becoming the de facto standard for provisioning.

column1: Name for the feature of Entra External ID that provides handy account management and SSO features for customers? (Acronym)
column3: Customer Identity and Access Management (CIAM) provides features such as self-service sign-up; profile management; password reset; and single sign-on (SSO) for customer-facing applications.

column1: SSE stands for?
column3: Secure Service Edge (SSE) is a cloud-delivered security model that combines various security services to protect users; devices; and data regardless of their location.

column1: Mneumonic for the 5 things Conditional Access considers?
column3: Risk/Application/Device/User/Location; Conditional Access policies evaluate these signals to determine whether to grant or block access to resources; or require additional verification steps.

column1: the probability that a given identity or account is compromised.
column3: User risk is calculated based on various factors; such as sign-in behavior; device health; and location anomalies; leaked credentials; to assess the likelihood that an identity has been compromised.

column1: the probability that a given sign-in, or authentication request, isn't authorized by the identity owner.
column3: Sign-in risk is determined by analyzing various signals; such as unfamiliar locations; atypical sign-in times; and impossible travel scenarios; to evaluate the legitimacy of a sign-in attempt.

column1: What is Microsoft's unified data governance and compliance platform called?
column3: Microsoft Purview provides a comprehensive set of tools and services to help organizations manage data governance; compliance; and risk management across their entire data estate.

column1: The term for the conditions that determine which access controls to use in Conditional Access?
column3: Assignments define the specific conditions; such as users; groups; devices; applications; location; or risk that trigger the evaluation of Conditional Access policies.

column1: Microsofts SSE solution/unifying term for both Microsoft Entra Internet Access and Microsoft Entra Private Access
column3: Zero Trust network; identity; and endpoint access controls so that you can secure access to any app or resource; from any location; device; or identity.

column1: SWG meaning?
column3: A Secure Web Gateway (SWG) is a security solution that protects users from web-based threats by enforcing corporate and regulatory policies; filtering malicious content; and monitoring web traffic.
